title: The formation radius of HCN in O-rich asymptotic giant branch stars
question: What is the formation radius of HCN in the inner circumstellar envelopes of the O-rich AGB stars R Crt and IK Tau, to shed light on nonequilibrium chemical processes?

data.angular_resolution: ~0.03 arcsec max (0.070'' x 0.029'' for R Crt, 0.047'' x 0.031'' for IK Tau with uniform weighting; restored HPBW 0.05'')
data.sensitivity: Continuum rms: 0.31 and 0.21 mJy beam^-1 (uniform weighting), 0.08 and 0.17 mJy beam^-1 (natural weighting) for R Crt and IK Tau

what.value: Stellar and circumstellar envelope parameters for IK Tau (V_sys, P, D, T_*, L_*, r_c, tau_10, T_d(r_c), M_dot, delta, v_inf, Psi)

evidence.quote: In the case of IK Tau, the parameters were taken from (cite: Massalkhi2024), while for R Crt we performed an analysis similar to that by these authors.

what.value: Near-infrared interferometric stellar radii for R Crt (9.0 mas) and IK Tau (10.35 mas)

evidence.quote: We favor the stellar radii derived from near-infrared interferometric observations (cite: Khouri2020; Adam2019) over the values inferred from $T_\star$ and $L_\star$ using the Stefan-Boltzmann law.

what.value: Distance, stellar effective temperature, systemic velocity, and terminal expansion velocity for R Crt

evidence.quote: Briefly, for R Crt we adopted the distance (cite: gaiadr3), stellar effective temperature (cite: Schoier2013), and terminal expansion velocity (cite: Massalkhi2020) from the literature

what.value: Observed velocity-integrated intensities of CO transitions (J=1-0, 2-1, 3-2, 4-3, 5-4, 9-8) in R Crt from SEST, APEX, and Herschel/HIFI

evidence.quote: by comparing the calculated velocity-integrated intensities with the observed intensities of multiple CO lines (see Table 3).
Table notes: (1) (cite: Kerschbaum1999). (2) (cite: Bergman2020), from APEX Pointing Catalogue. (3) (cite: Danilovich2015).

what.value: Initial HCN abundance f_0 (3.5e-7 for R Crt, 4.3e-7 for IK Tau) and empirical e-folding radius expression

evidence.quote: Following (cite: Schoier2013), the abundance distribution at the initial radius for R Crt and IK Tau are 3.5 $\times$ 10$^{-7}$ and 4.3 $\times$ 10$^{-7}$.
The $r_e$ value is evaluated through the empirical expression in Eq. (3) of (cite: Schoier2013) and are 1.0 $\times$ 10$^{16}$ cm and 2.0 $\times$ 10$^{16}$ cm for R Crt and IK Tau, respectively.

what.value: HCN spectroscopic parameters (HITRAN2020) and collisional rate coefficients with H2 and He

evidence.quote: The energy levels and radiative transition Einstein coefficients were taken from the HITRAN2020 database (cite: hitran).

The collisional downward rate coefficients for pure rotational transitions were taken from (cite: Hernandez-Vera2017) for collisions with a para/ortho H$_2$ (adopting an ortho-to-para ratio of 3) and from (cite: Dumouchel2010) for collisions with He

what.value: Line rest frequencies from the CDMS database

evidence.quote: Frequencies from the CDMS database <https://cdms.astro.uni-koeln.de>

recipe.goal: Measure continuum positions and radio photosphere sizes (R_mm)
recipe.method: Fit 2D Gaussian to non-self-calibrated natural-weighted 354 GHz continuum emission above 3 sigma using SciPy; take R_mm as half the FWHM
key_parameters: Frequency = 354 GHz; threshold > 3 sigma; natural weighting
assumptions: Radio photosphere is originated by free-free radiation that becomes optically thick at R_mm = FWHM / 2

recipe.goal: Model dusty circumstellar envelope of R Crt via SED fitting
recipe.method: Run a grid of 1D spherical continuum radiative transfer models with DUSTY V2 varying tau_10 and T_c, and find the best fit to VizieR photometric SED via reduced chi-squared
key_parameters: Spherical grains of radius 0.1 um; warm silicate optical properties from Suh (1999)
assumptions: Spherical dusty envelope; dust present only beyond condensation radius r_c with uniform gas-to-dust ratio; 20% uniform flux uncertainties

recipe.goal: Model gaseous envelope (mass loss rate and temperature profile) of R Crt via CO lines
recipe.method: Run a grid of non-LTE radiative transfer models for CO (v=0 and v=1) using modified RATRAN, varying mass loss rate and gas temperature exponent delta, and fit to archival single-dish/space CO line integrated intensities
key_parameters: CO fractional abundance = 2.0e-4 relative to H2; v_0 = v_inf / 4; beta = 1; photospheric pressure = 5e-5 bar; density exponent b = 2
assumptions: Spherical symmetry; power-law gas temperature T_g(r) = T_* (r/R_*)^-delta; 20% uniform uncertainties on CO intensities

recipe.goal: Constrain HCN formation radius (r_h) via non-LTE LVG radiative transfer modeling
recipe.method: Compute non-LTE LVG radiative transfer models of HCN (J=4-3 in v=0 and v2=1) with an inner abundance hole of radius r_h = 1 to 10 R_*, integrate over +/- 5 km s^-1 around V_sys, and compare with observed azimuthally averaged radial brightness profiles
key_parameters: r_h = 1 to 10 R_*; velocity integration range = V_sys +/- 5 km s^-1; f_0 = 3.5e-7 (R Crt) and 4.3e-7 (IK Tau); r_e = 1.0e16 cm (R Crt) and 2.0e16 cm (IK Tau); 41 rotational levels in v=0, v2=1, v2=2, v3=1, v1=1
assumptions: Gaussian HCN abundance fall-off beyond r_h; optically thick free-free radio photosphere between R_* and R_mm with ionization degree 1e-5; H2 ortho-to-para ratio of 3; He/H2 = 0.17; ro-vibrational collision rates scaled down by 10,000

score_reason: The observational setup, physical equations, input parameters (Table 1), photometric/CO data (Tables 2 and 3), and spectroscopic/collisional inputs are thoroughly documented, but the custom LVG and modified RATRAN codes are not publicly available and some GILDAS imaging/self-calibration parameters are omitted.
rediscovery_reason: The ALMA data (2019.1.00801.S) are public in the archive, the continuum photosphere sizes (R_mm) and HCN radial brightness peak positions (66 mas and 55 mas) can be directly re-measured from the ALMA visibilities/images, and the 1D radiative transfer hole-radius modeling is well-specified enough to be re-implemented with standard radiative transfer tools.
